summary.headline: Poultry losses are climbing again as fall migration peaks: APHIS confirmed 1.83 million layers in Okeechobee Co., FL (Nov 18) and big broiler flocks on the Delmarva Peninsula (Worcester Co., MD, 218,400; Sussex Co., DE, 269,900), Oklahoma has its first infected dairy herd since 2024, Oregon reported a dairy-linked human case (CDC total 75), and Canada now has 44 infected premises after a run of Saskatchewan and Fraser Valley outbreaks. In Jay's states, Utah lost a 1,400-bird backyard flock in Cache Co. (Nov 12), and new raptor cases include a bald eagle in Maricopa Co., AZ, great horned owls in Bonneville Co., ID and Laramie Co., WY, and a red-tailed hawk in Weber Co., UT.

notes.text: Raptors (APHIS wild-bird table, detected Nov 5–19): bald eagles in Maricopa Co., AZ (Nov 13), Park Co., MT (Nov 12) and Itasca Co., MN (Nov 5); great horned owls in Bonneville Co., ID and Laramie Co., WY (Nov 19), Oregon (Wallowa Co., Nov 5; county not given, Nov 16), Genesee Co., MI (Nov 13) and Stark Co., ND (Nov 12); red-tailed hawks in Weber Co., UT (Nov 9), Los Angeles Co., CA (Nov 12), Douglas Co., CO (Nov 13) and King Co., WA (Nov 19); and an unidentified falcon in Yolo Co., CA (Nov 13). A captive stork died of H5N1 at the Louisville Zoo, KY.

Dairy and people: Oklahoma's first infected herd since July 2024 was confirmed Nov 14 (county not released), making nine NMTS-affected states. Oregon reported its first human case of 2026 on Nov 19, a Morrow Co. worker with mild illness linked to the state's first infected dairy, bringing CDC's total to 75. Washington has 17 herds in 30 days; state ag and vet officials asked USDA on Nov 6 to fast-track a dairy-cow vaccination framework.

Jay's states: Utah lost a 1,400-bird backyard poultry flock in Cache Co. (Nov 12); Kansas's Greeley Co. flock (8,500, Nov 6) and South Dakota's Beadle Co. turkeys (Nov 4) are still active control areas. Wild birds in 30 days: Kansas 13 and Missouri 13 (mostly hunter-harvested ducks; MO adds teal in Chariton Co.), Utah 8, South Dakota 3, plus Arizona's bald eagle and Idaho's great horned owl; Idaho's Latah Co. wastewater had a low H5 positive Nov 9.

Canada: 24 new infected premises since Nov 6. Saskatchewan has nine small non-commercial flocks (Nov 10–21), several tied to a Nov 7 Moose Jaw poultry show that also seeded two Manitoba cases. BC's Fraser Valley has five commercial farms in November (Chilliwack ×2, Abbotsford, Surrey, Langley) plus a non-poultry site in Vancouver, Alberta six more incl. a commercial farm in Vulcan County, and Quebec a commercial farm in Les Maskoutains.

Wastewater: 36 CDC sites positive in the past 6 weeks; new hits since Nov 1 cluster in Oregon, Kittitas Co., WA (192,296 copies/L, Nov 11) and Alaska (Fairbanks, Juneau). The log reaches back the full 100 days to mid-August; APHIS's flock, wild-bird, mammal and livestock tables are read directly, wild birds aggregated by state and detection date.

lines: Netherlands (Friesland), Jan 2026: Europe's only dairy finding so far. Antibodies from a past infection in 34 of 72 lactating cows and 24 of 38 young stock, found after a farm cat died of H5N1. No virus in milk, no human infections.
Follow-up testing found no antibodies in more than 3,000 blood samples from other Dutch dairy farms.

Great Britain: H5N1 was found in a sheep's milk in Yorkshire in March 2025. APHA's 2024 survey of 508 bulk milk samples from 455 farms was all negative, and APHA rates the risk of a cattle-adapted strain reaching GB from the Netherlands as very low.
dairy.note: The Dutch herd was found through an investigation after the farm cat died, not through routine milk testing. Any EU or UK dairy herd detection will be added to the log and map.

europe.headline: Europe's wave keeps building: ADIS logged 102 wild-bird detections and 14 poultry outbreaks in Nov 12–18, with the Netherlands losing six more farms (incl. ~90,000 broilers at Tzummarum, Friesland, and ~60,000 layers at Oosterwolde), Norway eight laying-hen flocks traced to one supplier, and France raising its national risk to high with housing from Nov 20. In the UK, England has 14 commercial cases this season (two more on Nov 25 near Leominster and Frodsham), Northern Ireland reported its first at Cookstown, Wales and NI now require housing, and APHA rates the wild-bird risk very high.

notes.text: Raptors in ADIS Nov 12–18: Eurasian buzzards in the Netherlands, Belgium and Norway, a common kestrel and a peregrine falcon in the Netherlands, a peregrine in Belgium, a peregrine at Wieliszew (Masovian, Poland) and a Eurasian eagle-owl at Mežotne, Latvia. GB weeks 45–46 add a golden eagle in Highland (H5N5), a peregrine falcon in Somerset, a common buzzard in Flintshire (Wales's first wild-bird case of the season), a tawny owl in West Devon, a barn owl in the Scottish Borders and a sparrowhawk in Shropshire.

Netherlands: six more poultry farms since Nov 13 — a third at Hierden (~19,000 ducks and hens), Oosterwolde (~60,000 layers) and Ermelo (~11,000 ducks) in Gelderland, Tzummarum, Friesland (~90,000 broilers), and Collendoorn (Overijssel, 8,600 layers) and De Kwakel (North Holland) on Nov 23; the national housing order has applied since Oct 28.

Norway: eight commercial laying-hen outbreaks in November — Klepp (Nov 3), Vestby (Akershus, Nov 13), five flocks in Rogaland and Agder on Nov 15 and Lindesnes (Nov 17); Mattilsynet thinks seven trace to young hens from one supplier flock, and about 100,000 birds have been culled.

Housing and risk: France raised its national risk level to high (élevé) with mandatory housing from Nov 20; Germany's FLI raised its wild-bird and poultry-entry risk to high (Nov 9); Denmark (risk high, housing since Nov 9) and the Netherlands keep national housing. In the UK, Wales has an AIPZ from Nov 16 with housing from Nov 23, and Northern Ireland an AIPZ with housing from Nov 19.

UK: seven more English commercial cases since Nov 18 — Coningsby (Lincolnshire), Thirsk, Northallerton (North Yorkshire), Driffield (East Riding), a second Dereham premises (Norfolk), and Leominster (Herefordshire; zone reaches Wales) and Frodsham (Cheshire) on Nov 25. APHA now rates the wild-bird risk very high and the poultry risk high where biosecurity is poor.
